Rashi on Yoma 27a:1:1.hebrew: האי מבעיא ליה לגופיה - דניבעי כהן, ולא נלמד ממנו מיעוטא, ואם כן מנא לן שזרים כשרים להפשט וניתוח:
Rashi on Yoma 27a:1:1.english: This is needed for its own sake - that a priest is required [to bring the wood], [and one cannot derive from it] an exclusion; [if so,] from where do we know [that non-priests are fit] for flaying and cutting into pieces?:

Rashi on Yoma 27a:1:2.hebrew: דהוה מסבר ליה לבריה - הא דאמרן דחזקיה, והכי מסבר ליה ניהליה, דתניא בתורת כהנים: "ושחט" — שחיטה בזר כשירה:
Rashi on Yoma 27a:1:2.english: That he was explaining to his son - This [derivation] of Hizkiya, and so he explained it to him, as it was taught in Torat Kohanim: "And he shall slaughter" — slaughter by a non-priest is valid:

Rashi on Yoma 27a:1:3.hebrew: וכי מאין באת - לישנא דמתני' הוא: וכי מאין באת לומר פסולה, שנזקקת להביא מקרא להכשירה:
Rashi on Yoma 27a:1:3.english: "And from where did you come" - This is the language of a Mishnah [i.e., a baraita]: "And from where did you come [to think] that it is invalid," such that one needs to bring a verse to render it valid:

Rashi on Yoma 27a:1:4.hebrew: מכלל שנאמר כו' - ומתוך אותו כלל הייתי בא לפסול:
Rashi on Yoma 27a:1:4.english: From the general statement that is stated, etc. - And from that general statement I would have come to disqualify [slaughter by a non-priest]:

Rashi on Yoma 27a:2:1.hebrew: תלמוד לומר ושחט והקריבו הכהנים - ומדכתיב "כהן" בקבלה, ובשחיטה לא כתיב, מכלל דושחט אבעלים קאי. "וסמך ידו ושחט" - לימד על השחיטה שכשירה בזר, עכ"ל משנה, ומינה הוה מסבר אביי לבריה הא דחזקיה הכי:
Rashi on Yoma 27a:2:1.english: The verse states: "And he shall slaughter… and the priests shall sacrifice" - Since "priest" is written regarding the receiving [of the blood] but is not written regarding the slaughter, it follows that "and he shall slaughter" refers to the owner. "And he shall place his hand and he shall slaughter" teaches that the slaughter is valid when performed by a non-priest. [Here] ends the text of the teaching [the baraita], and from it Abaye would explain this statement of Chizkiyah to his son in this way:

Tosafot on Yoma 27a:2:1.hebrew: והקריבו בני אהרן מקבלה ואילך וכו' - בפ"ק דזבחים (ד' ד.) פרש"י: הא דאמרינן "והקריבו" זו קבלת הדם, ולא עבודה אחרת משאר עבודות דם, כגון הולכה או זריקה, משום דכתיב "ושחט והקריבו", ואיזו היא עבודה שהיא אחר שחיטה לאלתר? הוי אומר זו קבלה. והקשה ר"י דבספ"ק דזבחים איכא טעמא אחרינא, כדתניא התם: "והקריבו" זו קבלת הדם, או אינו אלא זריקה? כשהוא אומר "וזרקו" הרי זריקה אמור, הא מה אני מקיים "והקריבו" זו קבלת הדם. אלמא דלאו היינו טעמא. והא דלא אמרינן "זו הולכה", משום דלא מסתברא לאוקמיה בהולכה ולומר מהולכה ואילך מצות כהונה, משום דאפשר לבטלה, דאפשר עומד בצד מזבח ושוחט, דלא בעי להוליך:
Tosafot on Yoma 27a:2:1.english: "And the sons of Aaron shall sacrifice" — from the collection onward, etc. - In the first chapter of Zevachim (4a), Rashi explained: That which we say that "and they shall sacrifice" refers to the collection of the blood, and not another service from among the other blood services, such as carrying or sprinkling, is because it is written "and he shall slaughter, and they shall sacrifice"; and which service is it that comes immediately after slaughter? Say that this is the collection. But Rabbeinu Yitzchak raised a difficulty: at the end of the first chapter of Zevachim there is another reason, as it was taught there: "And they shall sacrifice" — this is the collection of the blood. Or perhaps it is only sprinkling? When it says "and they shall sprinkle," sprinkling is already stated; so how do I explain "and they shall sacrifice"? [As] the collection of the blood. Evidently, then, that is not the reason. And as for the fact that we do not say that ["and they shall sacrifice"] refers to carrying, it is because it is not reasonable to establish it as carrying and to say that from carrying onward is a mitzva of priesthood, because it can be nullified [as a requirement of priests], since it is possible [for the priest] to stand beside the altar and slaughter, so that he would not need to carry:

Tosafot on Yoma 27a:2:2.hebrew: אלא מהכא וערכו בני אהרן הכהנים - בפ' ב' דזבחים (ד' יח.) דריש "הכהנים בכיהונם": כהן הדיוט שלבש בגדי כ"ג ועבד עבודה, עבודתו פסולה. והכא דריש מדכתיב "בני אהרן". ואין להקשות: מאי איצטריך קרא לעריכת נתחים למילפה מדקאמר "מקבלה ואילך מצות כהונה"? תיפוק ליה מ"וכי תעלה על דעתך שזר קרב אצל המזבח"! די"ל דאפשר דקאי בארעא וזריק להו למזבח, כדאי' לקמן בס"פ טרף בקלפי גבי הצתת אליתא: אפשר דקאי אארעא ועביד במפוחא:
Tosafot on Yoma 27a:2:2.english: Rather, from here: "And the sons of Aaron the priests shall arrange" - In the second chapter of Zevachim (18a) it expounds "the priests" [to mean] "in their priesthood": an ordinary priest who put on the garments of the High Priest and performed a service, his service is invalid. And here it expounds [this] from the fact that it is written "the sons of Aaron." And one should not ask: Why was a verse needed to derive [the requirement of priests for] the arranging of the pieces, from [the Gemara's] statement "from the collection [of the blood] onward is a mitzva of priesthood"? Let it derive it from "Could it enter your mind that a non-priest approaches the altar?" For one can answer that it is possible that he stands on the ground and throws them onto the altar, as stated below at the end of chapter Taraf BaKalpi regarding the kindling of the fat tail: It is possible that he stands on the ground and does [it] with a bellows:
